name: nordvpn
description: NordVPN on macOS through Tunnelblick (OpenVPN, no sudo): status and server lists are free; connect/disconnect preview until --yes and leave an audit line; service credentials from env, a 600-mode file, or the Keychain — never the tree
surface: CLI. `status`/`servers`/`countries`/`configs` read; `connect`/`disconnect` print a preview and exit 0 until re-run with `--yes` (flag tier: the tunnel is this machine's own and reversible), then append to `data/audit.log`; no account, billing, or server-side verb exists

origin.note: hello-* workshop repo; the belt added the --yes gate, previews, audit log, hostname validation, the credential stores, moved the staged .tblk bundles out of the tree, and made `status` stop launching Tunnelblick. Upstream gitignored poetry.lock; the belt's lockfile is its own

install.run: poetry env use python3.13 && poetry install
install.description: Create the in-project .venv and install httpx, typer, pydantic, rich, python-dotenv from poetry.lock
install.why: the CLI imports these; poetry.toml pins the venv to tools/nordvpn/.venv so nothing is installed globally
install.yes: tools/nordvpn/.venv is created from the committed lockfile; no call to NordVPN is made
install.no: skipped; every `poetry run nordvpn` fails on import until you run it

install.description: Create the directory where downloaded OpenVPN bundles are staged before Tunnelblick imports them
install.why: each .tblk bundle embeds the service credentials, so it must live outside the repo
install.no: skipped; connect --yes creates it on first use anyway

env.name: NORD_USER
env.description: NordVPN OpenVPN service username (from the manual-configuration page, not the account login). Alternatives: ~/.config/toolbelt/nordvpn.env (mode 600) or Keychain item toolbelt-nordvpn/NORD_USER. Needed only by connect

env.name: NORD_PASS
env.description: NordVPN OpenVPN service password. Same alternatives as NORD_USER

env.name: NORDVPN_CONFIG_DIR
env.description: Where downloaded .ovpn files and credential-bearing .tblk bundles are staged (default ~/.config/toolbelt/nordvpn/configs, mode 700)

auth.flow: The operator's own NordVPN service credentials, generated once on the NordVPN dashboard; the public server API needs no token. Read from NORD_USER/NORD_PASS, else ~/.config/toolbelt/nordvpn.env (600 enforced), else Keychain toolbelt-nordvpn, else the deprecated in-tree .env (warned). Never printed
auth.login: security add-generic-password -s toolbelt-nordvpn -a NORD_USER -w <username> && security add-generic-password -s toolbelt-nordvpn -a NORD_PASS -w <password>

caches.note: optional dotenv file with NORD_USER/NORD_PASS; refused unless mode 600
caches.revoke: Regenerate the service credentials on https://my.nordaccount.com/dashboard/nordvpn/manual-configuration/ and delete the file

caches.note: staged .tblk bundles, each with a 600-mode .pass file holding the service credentials; dir 700
Tunnelblick's own copy of every imported bundle, credentials included
caches.revoke: delete the configuration in Tunnelblick's VPN Details window

safeguards: Read-first: status, servers, countries, configs and setup mutate nothing; only connect and disconnect change the tunnel, and no verb touches the NordVPN account, billing, or any server-side state (SENSIBILITIES #1)

connect and disconnect are flag-gated (cli.py, `yes: YesOpt`): a bare call prints the preview — server, whether a credential-bearing bundle will be installed, what is replaced, the timeout, the undo — and exits 0 having changed nothing; --yes is always honored because the tunnel is this machine's own and `disconnect --yes` undoes it (SENSIBILITIES #2)

Every mutation appends `[nordvpn audit] <ts> verb= target= result=` to stderr and data/audit.log (audit.py, file 600, dir 700): connect, disconnect, and the config install connect performs (SENSIBILITIES #7)
Ceilings are constants in cli.py: MAX_LIMIT 50 on `servers --limit` (refused above, not lowered), DEFAULT_LIMIT 10, CONNECT_TIMEOUT_S 30 (SENSIBILITIES #3)

Server hostnames and country codes are validated before use (config_manager.normalize_hostname, cli._country_code); a config name with a quote never reaches the AppleScript string TunnelblickController.connect builds

Credentials resolve env → ~/.config/toolbelt/nordvpn.env → Keychain → in-tree .env (credentials.get_credentials); a group/world-readable file is refused, the in-tree file is warned on, and no path prints a value — Credentials.__repr__ masks both (SENSIBILITIES #6, #11)
Downloaded bundles embed the service credentials, so ConfigManager stages them under ~/.config/toolbelt/nordvpn/configs (mode 700, .pass 600), never under the tool dir (SENSIBILITIES #11)

Degraded modes are named: status reports 'Tunnelblick not running' without launching it, `--local` skips the off-host IP lookups, and a failed ipify/ipinfo call prints 'unavailable' instead of failing the read (SENSIBILITIES #8)

verbs.name: status
verbs.note: Tunnelblick state; without --local also fetches the public IP from api.ipify.org and geolocates it at ipinfo.io (sends the IP off-host)

verbs.name: servers
verbs.note: api.nordvpn.com recommendations for a country; --limit capped at MAX_LIMIT 50

verbs.name: configs
verbs.note: Tunnelblick's installed NordVPN configurations via AppleScript

verbs.name: setup
verbs.note: pre-flight: launches Tunnelblick if needed, resolves credentials (presence only), one API read

verbs.name: connect
verbs.note: preview without --yes; with --yes may download an .ovpn, bundle it with the credentials, hand it to Tunnelblick (its own import dialog), then connect; reversible with disconnect --yes

verbs.name: disconnect
verbs.note: preview without --yes; with --yes tells Tunnelblick to disconnect all; reversible with connect --yes

verbs.name: account / billing / server-side changes
verbs.note: no verb exists; the tool holds service credentials only, which cannot act on the account

verbs.name: delete configuration
verbs.note: no verb; remove bundles in Tunnelblick's VPN Details window

risk.worst_case: this Mac's traffic is routed through (or out of) a NordVPN server the operator did not mean, after a --yes; `status` reveals the public IP to ipify/ipinfo; a credential-bearing .tblk lands under ~/.config/toolbelt/nordvpn/configs and inside Tunnelblick

checks.label: service credentials resolvable (env, 600-mode file, or Keychain; presence only)

smoke_test.command: poetry run nordvpn --help >/dev/null && poetry run python -m unittest discover -s tests -q
smoke_test.expect: help renders; unit tests pass with no network, no credential, no Tunnelblick: tiers match the manifest, hostname validation, the --limit ceiling, credential-store order and mode refusal, audit line format, connect/disconnect preview without --yes
